newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Socialists to vote against 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Socialists to vote against 1997 budget.

text.p: In a symbolic protest, Spain's Socialists announced on Monday they would vote against the conservative government's 1997 draft budget.

The draft, presented 10 days ago, is guaranteed to be approved by parliament, where the minority ruling Popular Party (PP) counts with the support of the Catalan Convergence and Unity (CiU) coalition.
The Socialist Workers' Party (PSOE) accused the PP over the weekend of cheating in its 1997 budget so Spain could join a single European currency.
"This is the most trick-laden budget ever submitted to parliament," Jose Borrell, the top Socialist in the congressional budget committee, said on Saturday.
The PSOE's executive committee ratified on Monday the decision to vote against the budget, which Borrell had announced over the weekend.
The former Socialist administration was forced to rollover the 1995 budget after its 1996 draft proposals were rejected by parliament last year.
